# Independent audit: marked entropy and its entire superdifferential

Source: `candidate 0e1bf4bac5d35265`.
Full independent analytic read of Sections1–7: **PASS. No correction
identified.** This audit concerns marked entropy, not an optimized mixed-depth
derivative. The separately audited sampled-majorant construction is correct.

## 1. The new uniform bound from marked values alone

Every nonzero conditional tilted row on a positive fiber is absolutely
continuous and has its centroid strictly inside that fiber. Otherwise a
supporting affine functional would vanish almost surely, contradicting
absolute continuity and positive conditional mass. There are only finitely
many positive row/fiber pairs, so a common small contraction about these
conditional centroids maps their old fiber supports into the current fibers.
Its full row mean stays EXACTLY Y_i because the conditional centroid average
equals the original row mean.

Row Jensen therefore gives (8) at the unchanged marked constraints. The
estimate U(x)>=dist(x,boundary K) max U/diam K follows by extending the line
from a maximizer through x to the opposite boundary point. Every image of a
fixed old core stays in a common current core. Summing q_i=1 on that old core
then bounds each current sampled maximum. No regularity, derivative or
uniform lower bound on the allocation densities is used. The contractions
serve only this bound, not the body derivative.

## 2. Local positive attainment

The legal finite-plane old comparison parameter supplies a lower entropy
bound near (C,l). Together with uniform upper maxima and positive fiber
volumes, this prevents any entire fiber maximum from tending to zero.
Concave homothetic superlevel sets then give logarithmic uniform
integrability, including moving boundary collars.

Bounded sampled touching majorants preserve feasibility and increase entropy.
Their coefficient limits are nonnegative, positive on fiber interiors, and
retain all marked bounds. Log UI passes the objective to the limit. The old
certificate, extended by V+delta L and monotone/dominated logarithmic passage
if necessary, forces that limit to equal L on every sampled fiber, including
its boundary. Marks have positive limiting values because they lie inside
positive limiting fibers; zero old certificate weights present no exception.

This subsequential rigidity gives the claimed common positive floor for
nearby maximizing envelopes. The explicit contradiction argument establishing
local positive attainment is valid: if nearby maximizing coefficient limits
were necessarily boundary-zero, choose nearly maximizing planes approaching
such limits along data converging to (C,l). Their uniform limiting positivity
would contradict the preceding rigidity. This does not assert global positive
attainment for arbitrary marked data.

## 3. Both directions of the moving-domain comparison

The bounded finite-plane maximizers extend positively to a common neighborhood
of the old hull and satisfy the SAME marked bounds on old and new bodies.
Thus a current maximizer is an old competitor, and conversely an old maximizer
for b(t) is a current competitor. Their uniform sampled-boundary convergence
to L lets one replace their logarithms by the fixed boundary integrand with
o(1) times O(t) error. The signed shell term is -t s(v) for the current-minus-old
integral. This proves the two-sided entropy comparison (11), with no derivative
of the parameters or row pushes hidden in the coefficient.

## 4. Exact supergradient-to-martingale converse

H is finite on the positive orthant: a constant competitor gives a lower
bound, and the old certificate gives the global logarithmic upper bound.
Mixing feasible concave parameters and using log concavity proves concavity
of H. Hence its interior superdifferential is nonempty and compact.

A supergradient g is nonnegative by monotonicity. Testing the exact scaling
law in both signs yields sum g_i l_i=1. For every radial feasible parameter
direction h, differentiating only the elementary fixed positive integral
gives (12). Both signs of affine h give equality of total masses and ALL
ambient first moments between sum g_i delta_Yi and dm/(ML). Taking h=-phi
for each continuous convex phi gives the correct convex-order direction.
The cited finite-source allocation theorem therefore applies, including
zero g_i. Its source and target L moments are both one. Concave Jensen makes
every positive row L-tight, so sigma_i=g_i l_i is exactly a certificate (1).
This proves the converse, not merely inclusion of known certificates in the
superdifferential.

## 5. Directional value and normalization

The concave directional derivative is the MINIMUM of the old supergradients
on the specified direction. The proof using bounded new supergradients has
the correct signs and retains all certificate choices. Local Lipschitz
continuity allows o(t) changes of the marked bounds. Combining this with
the signed body-domain comparison gives (4). Multiplying by M/M_t changes
its first-order value only by o(t), because the base entropy value is zero
and the perturbed value is O(t).

Nothing in this argument identifies the marked entropy response with the
derivative of the full buffered-depth optimum. Actual scalar cap responses,
supporting statuses and the relation to physical body variations remain
separate, as the source states.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
